items.title: Could Toronto Pearson Airport privatization create a new mini ‘city’ in Mississauga?
items.summary: In recent days, you may have heard of the federal government’s plan to bring in a private operator to run Toronto Pearson International Airport, and if you are a Mississauga resident, your first thought might be higher fees, more noise, and potentially fewer jobs. But this may not be the whole story of what could be happening at the airport. While talk of potential privatization is new and there are myriad uncertainties–especially regarding how much input and influence the city will have–there’s also a great deal of economic potential. While Pearson has a number of shops and restaurants, a new model could herald the creation of an airport city–the kind you see in Asia and Europe that feels more like a mini urban enclave than a transit hub. During my time at the Greater Toronto Airports Authority, I always noticed the airport’s true value hiding in plain sight: its location. Pearson sits on 1,867 hectares of federal land inside Canada’s seventh-largest city, at the centre of Canada’s second-largest employment zone. According to a 2025 Deloitte study for the GTAA, the zone offers more than 500,000 jobs, many of them in Mississauga. It boasts robust transit connectivity, offering access to the 401, 427, 409 and 407, the Kitchener GO line and the UP Express. For an institutional investor, this is the underlying fact that could turn the airport from a natural monopoly business into a potential growth-based investment. Pearson is currently managed by a federal not-for-profit, the GTAA, which already runs a bespoke private model. It leases the land, then builds, maintains and operates its buildings and runways, generating revenue for growth and upkeep. This is not dissimilar to what the federal government is proposing right now. Whether you like or dislike this model, you must be asking what changes with Prime Minister Mark Carney’s plan.

items.title: Nine-tower development at Mississauga mall approved in Ontario Land Tribunal settlement
items.summary: A nine-tower mixed-use development at a Mississauga mall has been approved under an Ontario Land Tribunal settlement. The plan is for a property in the northwest quadrant of Erin Mills Town Centre at 5100 Erin Mills Parkway. The property is currently home to restaurants and shops, which would be torn down for the development. , was planning a multi-phased development with nine towers, from 20 to 44 storeys high, with a total of 3,162 units. Residents opposed the project when it came to public meetings in 2025. People raised concerns about the height of the buildings, the lack of proposed affordable and rental units, and the loss of existing retail businesses. The property owner appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, citing council’s failure to make a decision on the official plan amendment and rezoning applications. The tribunal has the power to override municipal decisions. The city and the developer reached a settlement, which the tribunal approved in a decision released last week. The revised plan is for nine mixed-use tower-on-podium buildings ranging from 20 to 37 storeys in height, a public park, an urban plaza and a pedestrian and road network. The project would be built in phases. A chart shows the differences between the original proposal and new proposal for 5100 Erin Mills Parkway. com.

items.title: ‘Distinctive and memorable’ park considered for downtown core in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga is moving ahead with an early stages plan that could lead to the development of a “distinctive and memorable public space” in the city’s downtown core. City council decided on Tuesday to enter into a memorandum of understanding with developer Camrost Felcor “for the purpose of exploring enhanced park design for city-owned property” at the southwest corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Kariya Drive. The green space is adjacent to the site being developed by Camrost Felcor and located directly north of Kariya Park, the tranquil Japanese-style park named for Mississauga’s sister city located southwest of Tokyo. ” If it does come to fruition, the new park, at just under one acre in size, would be significantly smaller than Kariya Park. In the conclusion of his report, Raj Sheth, the City of Mississauga’s commissioner of community services, said “the new park’s close proximity to Kariya Park, which is recognized as one of the city’s treasured public spaces, provides an opportunity to complement and enhance the broader park experience in this area of the Downtown Core.

items.title: Mississauga Council Orders Study Into Portable Washrooms for Its Busiest Parks
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga city council voted Tuesday to direct staff toward studying whether portable washrooms could be added to some of the city's busiest parks. The motion, dubbed the Porta-Potties in Parks Pilot Program, asks staff to investigate the feasibility of a seasonal portable washroom pilot at select high-use parks. Ward 4 Councillor John Kovac introduced the motion after hearing years of complaints from residents frustrated by the lack of convenient washroom access while visiting green spaces. Kovac noted that only some of the city's larger parks currently offer any bathroom facilities, since permanent structures come with a steep price tag. He argued that amenities like shelters and seating are common in Mississauga parks, but washrooms remain largely absent for that reason. In pitching the idea, Kovac pointed to Ottawa, Toronto and Hamilton as examples of cities that have already rolled out similar portable washroom programs. He called the proposal a small step for council that could bring a big relief for park visitors. Staff are now expected to report back on whether a pilot program is workable before any portable units are installed.

items.title: The Ontario SPCA brings spay/neuter and wellness services to Mississauga FN
items.summary: More than 50 animals received veterinary care during a three-day spay/neuter and wellness event in Mississauga First Nation, helping local families access important care for their animal companions. A total of 18 dogs and 5 cats were spayed or neutered during the Sept. 23-25 MASH-style event. The surgeries will help prevent more than an estimated 1,100 potentially unplanned puppies and kittens. The event also provided 29 animal wellness appointments, giving people access to veterinary care close to home. Animals received veterinary examinations and, where needed, vaccinations and other preventive care. “On behalf of Mississauga First Nation, I would like to extend our deepest gratitude to the Ontario SPCA vets, staff and volunteers for everything they do, both here and across the province of Ontario,” says Scott Richer, Bylaw Services Officer, Mississauga First Nation. ” The Ontario SPCA’s MASH-style clinics bring veterinary services directly into communities where access to care can be challenging. The mobile model allows the Ontario SPCA to pack up the equipment and resources needed to provide spay/neuter and wellness services and take them wherever they are needed. Spaying and neutering can help prevent unplanned litters and supports the health and well-being of animals. By combining spay/neuter surgeries with wellness appointments, these community events provide an opportunity for animals to receive important veterinary care in one place. “Bringing veterinary care directly into communities helps remove barriers and makes it easier for families to access the care their animals need,” says Arista Wogenstahl, Northern Regional Manager of Community Outreach Services, Ontario SPCA and Humane Society. ” The Ontario SPCA is committed to working with communities to help remove barriers to veterinary care and keep people and their animal companions together.

items.title: Road Closures Follow Fatal Hit-and-Run Involving Pickup Truck in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CBC Toronto and Insauga, a pedestrian died Tuesday evening after being hit by a pickup truck in a hit and run at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West in Mississauga. Peel Regional Police say the victim, an adult, was struck by the vehicle and pronounced dead at the scene, though officers have not released further details about who was killed. A spokesperson with Peel Regional Paramedic Services confirmed only that the victim was an adult. Police shut down all eastbound and westbound lanes on Dundas Street between Hampshire Gate and Woodchester Drive through the Winston Churchill intersection while investigators worked the scene. Drivers in the area faced significant delays, and police urged motorists to avoid the intersection while emergency crews remained on site. Peel Regional Police are asking anyone with information about the crash to call their non-emergency line at 905-453-3311.
